newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Minister denies role in cash-for-vote scam.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Minister denies role in cash-for-vote scam.

text.p: Brazil Communications Minister Sergio Motta denied any role in an alleged cash-for-votes scheme in which congressmen reportedly accepted bribes in exchange for voting for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's reelection bid.

Speaking at a news conference Motta said an article published in Wednesday's Folha de Sao Paulo daily that suggested he might be linked to the alleged vote buying scheme was libelous and irresponsible.
"I reject and do not recognize any of the statements transcribed in the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper," Motta told reporters.
"There is no accusation or hard evidence," he said.

On Tuesday Folha published a transcript of a conversation in which a congressman allegedly claimed he and four other deputies had accepted $188,000 in exchange for voting for Cardoso's reelection bid.
In Wednesday edition the newspaper alleged new tapes suggested the money was paid with Motta's blessing.
A close friend and private business partner of President Cardoso, Motta is widely considered among the most influential members in the cabinet.
Responsible for overseeing an $80 billion telecommunications privatization plan, Motta is widely considered as the president's main political operator and the architect of his reelection bid.
Visibly angry and upset, Motta attacked Folha de Sao Paulo saying this kind of journalism reminded him of the propaganda tactics of Nazi Germany.
"I understand the headline of the story to be deceptive, libelous, with hidden design and with strange political objectives," Motta said.
Motta said that on Thursday he would prosecute the congressmen who allegedly mentioned his name in the taped conversations.
